integrity: The proof uses Jagiella’s finite-dimensional reduction to a one-dimensional \(\omega,<\)-quotient and then only minimality plus the definition of algebraic closure. Every fixed quotient level is definable over the same finite parameter tuple and is finite, so every home-sort element is algebraic over that tuple. No computational evidence is used.
scientific_limitations: The theorem is only a necessary condition for interpreting \(\omega,<\); finite-parameter algebraicity does not imply interpretability. The conclusion concerns the home sort, not all imaginaries or all elements of a monster model, and the proof uses definability of individual positions in \(\omega,<\).
title: Interpreting \(\omega\) forces finite-parameter algebraicity in minimal structures
